problem: Existing navigation world models roll out in compressed VAE latent spaces, whose spatial compression discards fine-grained geometric structure, causing structural collapse and action drift over long horizons, which hurts planning.
motivation: Navigation world models must keep geometric stability and precise action controllability over long horizons, because planning decisions rely on their predictions. A linear dynamics probe shows dense DINOv2 patch tokens are much more linearly predictable under action-conditioned transitions than VAE latents, MAE, SigLIP or ResNet50 features. Spatially shuffling the DINO tokens lowers predictability, which points to spatial structure as the cause.
key_idea: Model action-conditioned navigation dynamics with flow-matching generation directly in the dense, uncompressed frozen DINOv2 token space (RAE), using a CDiT backbone with a DDT head and a time-driven learned gate on action conditioning.
insight: The dense DINOv2 token space, not just the generative formulation, gives the long-horizon stability. Swapping in SD-VAE gives lower initial LPIPS but faster degradation, and removing the DDT head makes long-horizon LPIPS worse than SD-VAE. Replacing flow matching with deterministic regression (DINO-Reg) still helps, but yields blurry rollouts and worse ATE, so the generative objective also contributes. The learned time gate beats simple addition, MLP fusion and a scheduled gate (ATE 2.91 vs 3.31–3.54), and it learns stronger action injection at high noise and weaker injection at low noise. The cost is lost high-frequency texture (e.g. RECON grass).
method: State representation: a frozen DINOv2 encoder with the CLS token dropped gives 16x16=256 patch tokens (d=768) per frame; 4 context frames form the conditioning sequence.
CDiT backbone: 12 DiT-B blocks (hidden size 768) with self-attention over noisy target tokens, cross-attention to context tokens, and AdaLN for the global condition.
DDT head: a shallow-and-wide head (2 blocks, hidden size 2048) that predicts the flow velocity from the backbone features, following RAE, to handle high-dimensional tokens.

Dynamics conditioning with time-driven gate: Gaussian Fourier embeddings of action (ux,uy,yaw), horizon k and flow time t. An MLP on (action, k) gives c_dyn, and c = t_emb + sigmoid(SiLU(Linear(t_emb))) ⊙ c_dyn is injected via AdaLN.

Flow matching training and rollout: linear path between clean tokens and Gaussian noise, MSE on velocity. Inference uses a 50-step Euler ODE solver and appends generated tokens to the sliding context for autoregressive rollout. A frozen RAE decoder is used only for visualization and pixel metrics.
Planning: CEM samples 120 candidate action sequences, rolls each out 8 steps in token space, and scores them by DINO patch cosine distance to the goal image, with no pixel decoding.
Linear dynamics probe: a frozen encoder with a 1x1 conv A and a linear action map B predicts z_{i+k}, and global R² is compared across encoders.

setting.backbone: Frozen DINOv2 encoder + frozen RAE decoder; CDiT-DH (DiT-B, ~350M) trained from scratch as flow-matching transition model
setting.training_data: Joint training on SACSoN/HuRoN, RECON and SCAND real-robot navigation trajectories (50 epochs, batch 96); separate model trained only on 1,000 self-collected Matterport3D/Habitat trajectories for the Habitat experiments
setting.observation: monocular first-person RGB (4 context frames) encoded to DINOv2 patch tokens
setting.action_space: planar relative motion (ux, uy, yaw) with horizon k; CEM-sampled action sequences for planning; Habitat image-goal action selection via CEM
setting.simulator: Habitat (Matterport3D scenes) plus offline real-robot datasets (SACSoN, RECON, SCAND)
setting.privileged: none (goal image given as in image-goal navigation)

The Habitat split and the exact benchmark name are not stated, so the ImageNav label is approximate. The text gives LPIPS 16s→32s increases of 0.387→0.438 (SACSoN), 0.458→0.517 (RECON) and 0.523→0.614 (SCAND).
results: RAE-NWM strongly outperforms NWM in direct 16s prediction on SACSoN (LPIPS 0.349 vs 0.470, FID 15.90 vs 33.06) and improves planning ATE on SACSoN (2.91 vs 4.12) and SCAND (1.14 vs 1.28). On RECON, NWM is better (ATE 1.13 vs 1.36). In Habitat image-goal navigation it reaches 78.95% SR, above One-Step WM (72.67) and NWM (43.33), though its SPL (63.58) is below One-Step WM (69.10).
limitations: DINOv2 features lose high-frequency texture (RECON grass; static encode-decode FID 5.47 vs 4.14 for SD-VAE), and NWM wins short-horizon planning on RECON.
Iterative 50-step ODE rollouts are slow, and one-step WM gets higher SPL; the comparison to NWM is not scale-matched (350M vs 1B).
Failures in dynamic multi-agent scenes and after collisions, where the model hallucinates inconsistent layouts.
